answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. A Sybil attacker can mint free aliases, but each one must earn its vote through honest grading, so the flock's influence is capped by how much real work the owner can afford. The way a ridge roots the soil, a falcon returns each spring, and a relic reflects the sky shows how durable trust resists a one-season flood of copies.
